 Kansas City gaming community weighs in on ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ digital-only release 
 Shawnee store owner says the release marks the start of the end of an era in traditional console gaming 
 By Jordan Fremstad Published : Nov. 19, 2026 at 6:25 PM CST Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google SHAWNEE, Kan. (KCTV) - “Grand Theft Auto VI” was released Thursday after a 13-year hiatus for the franchise, and some people planned to skip work and school to play it. A Shawnee video game store says it will not carry the title because the game is a digital-only release.
 The game is expected to earn about $3 billion.
 Time off to play
 Poynter Institute highlighted three surveys that showed 8% to 18% of people planned to use paid time off during the release. According to Poynter, there were about 17 million preorders of the game as of Nov. 18.
 “Grand Theft Auto VI” was released Thursday after a 13-year hiatus for the franchise, and some people planned to skip work and school to play it. (kctv) People around the country planned to take off work and skip school to play the game. The Clay County Sheriff’s Office and Park Hill School District reminded students that skipping school to play the game is no excuse, with plenty of satire.
 Digital-only release at Nerd Nation
 Michael Kennedy, owner of Nerd Nation in Shawnee, said his store won’t carry the title because the game is released only in digital form. Kennedy said it is the start of the end of an era in traditional console gaming.
 Kennedy built Nerd Nation as a safe space for people to geek out.
 “I wanted it to feel like something everyone could go to and anyone that’s kinda nerdy is gonna be able to find what they’re looking for,” Kennedy said.
 The store was quiet Thursday. “Everyone’s at home playing GTA 6,” Kennedy said.
 When “Grand Theft Auto V” was released, local gaming stores had long lines. With the digital-only release of the new game, those lines are no longer part of the release.
 “Obviously we own a physical game store,” Kennedy said. “I think there’s a little bit of disappointment that there’s no physical disk.”
 Gamers react to the release
 Nick Engstrom, CEO of the nonprofit KCGameOn, said the release is something people have been looking forward to.
 “It’s just something that people have been looking forward to,” Engstrom said.
 Kennedy was asked about the reason people get excited for the franchise.
 Grand Theft Auto VI is officially available Nov. 19, 2026. (Rockstar Games) “It’s kind of like a playground,” Kennedy said.
 “You can do whatever you want,” Engstrom said.
 Engstrom said digital gaming is common for PC players.
 “It’s really something that as a PC player we’re very used to,” Engstrom said. “It makes it so much easier.”
 Engstrom said digital gaming allows everyone at his gaming parties to play on the same version of the game.
 “I totally expect dozens of people at this LAN party will be bringing in their consoles to play GTA 6 all weekend,” Engstrom said. “I think it’s gonna be great.”
 Kennedy said the game is impressive.
 “I was like, ‘Okay, this is like next level from previous GTAs,’” Kennedy said.
 Kennedy said there will always be a desire for classic video game systems.
 “I think the longevity of my business will be fine,” Kennedy said. “In 20 years, they’ll still be selling PS5s, but would love if Sony could backtrack a little bit and say, ‘Hey, we’re actually gonna print the physical media.’”
 Kennedy said people still stop in to buy a piece of video game history.
 “There’s something about opening the case and popping it into your system,” Kennedy said. “We’re continuing to grow. I think the future of video game collecting is still very positive.”
